diagnostic_evidence.quote: The remaining eigenvalues are given by those of $I_\sizeA+\alpha{A}^{-\ell} (I_\sizeA-\alpha{A}^{-\ell})^{-1}$

issues.failure_explanation: The non-unit eigenvalues of the preconditioned matrix are those of I_N + A^{-ell} Z_alpha^{-1}, equivalently I_N + alpha A^{-ell}(I_N - alpha A^{-ell})^{-1}. The proof of the corollary instead discusses the ordering of eigenvalues of I_N + A^{-ell} Z_alpha, which does not have the displayed eigenvalues mu_j^ell/(mu_j^ell - alpha). As written, the monotonicity argument is attached to the wrong matrix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Z_alpha by Z_alpha^{-1} in the proof, or invoke the eigenvalue formula from Theorem thm:evals directly; no change to the corollary statement or advertised regime is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the extreme-eigenvalue corollary is defective; the stated minimum and maximum eigenvalues are not justified by the written argument, although the eigenvalue formula from the preceding theorem is correct.
issues.title: Corollary proof refers to I_N + A^{-ell} Z_alpha instead of I_N + A^{-ell} Z_alpha^{-1}
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof-line repair that restores the intended argument and preserves the corollary statement, parameter regime, and downstream use.

issues.failure_explanation: The radical needed for the inequality is sqrt{(a^2 - b^2 - 1)^2 + 4a^2 b^2}. Algebraically this equals sqrt{(a^2 + b^2 - 1)^2 + 4 b^2}, not sqrt{(a^2 + b^2 - 1)^2 + 4 a^2 b^2}. The displayed simplification is therefore not equivalent to the preceding inequality, and the proof does not establish the required strict inequality as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the simplification to sqrt{(a^2 + b^2 - 1)^2 + 4 b^2} > a^2 + b^2 - 1, or use the valid appended derivation; the theorem statement and its use need no substantive change.
issues.overall_effect: The bound rho(lambda_j) < sigma_j, which supports the resource-allocation heuristic, is not justified by the main-body proof as written.
issues.title: Incorrect algebraic simplification in the complex Chebyshev convergence-factor proof
issues.why_classification: The defect is a contained algebraic error in the proof; a short correction preserves the stated bound, its regime, and all dependent uses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The corresponding saddle point problem for \eqref{eq:blockproblem} is then given by

issues.failure_explanation: Let u = Re(x_j), y = -Im(x_j), c = Re(b_j), d = Im(b_j), r = Re(lambda_j), s = Im(lambda_j). The displayed saddle system gives s u + (A - r I)y = -c and (A - r I)u - s y = d. The original complex system (A - (r + i s)I)x_j = b_j is equivalent to s u + (A - r I)y = -d and (A - r I)u - s y = c. Thus the real and imaginary right-hand sides are interchanged, and the displayed system generally solves a different problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the saddle system with a correct realification, for example using the right-hand side [-Im(b_j); Re(b_j)] for the positive-imaginary orientation and the corresponding sign-adjusted system for negative-imaginary roots, then revalidate the P_SP experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The real saddle-point construction underlying P_SP is not a valid reformulation of the complex inner problems as written, so the theoretical guarantees and numerical claims for P_SP that rely on solving eq:saddlesystem are unreliable.
issues.title: Saddle-point reformulation does not solve the original complex shifted system
issues.why_classification: This is more than a local typo: it invalidates the stated equivalence of a main proposed method and its associated numerical claims. A contained correction exists, but it requires repairing the construction and rechecking the P_SP results, so the least adequate resolution is moderate rather than minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We recall that $\mu_{\min} > {\Re({\lambda_j})}$, as the shifted systems lie in the right-half plane. Therefore $\psimat$ is invertible.
For complex roots $\lambda_{j}$, $j \in [2,\ell/2]\cup [\ell/2+2,\ell]$, we solve \eqref{eq:saddlesystem} using MINRES

issues.failure_explanation: In the displayed saddle matrix, Phi = Im(lambda_j) I. For the complex roots with negative imaginary part included in the stated range j in [2,ell/2] union [ell/2+2,ell], Phi is negative definite, contradicting the claim that Phi is symmetric positive definite. The proof also only establishes invertibility of Psi = A - Re(lambda_j) I and does not establish invertibility of P_D = Phi + Psi. For example, for lambda = conj(lambda_2) with alpha = 1, Phi + Psi = A - 1.397 I, which is not guaranteed to be invertible from the stated assumptions.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of the preconditioned system $\mathcal{P}_{D}^{-1}\mathcal{S}$ lie in  $\big[-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big] \cup \big[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},1\big]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict or restate the theorem for sign-adjusted systems in which the diagonal SPD block is |Im(lambda_j)| I, and add the required invertibility (or positive-definiteness) condition on Phi + Psi; negative-imaginary roots can then be covered by the corresponding conjugate or sign-changed real system.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue clustering guarantee for the MINRES saddle-point preconditioner is unsupported for the negative-imaginary complex subproblems that the paper says are solved by the same saddle-point formulation.
issues.title: Saddle-point eigenvalue theorem invoked outside its sign and invertibility hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The advertised spectral bound can be preserved by a local sign/orientation adjustment and a standard invertibility condition; no major loss of result or new proof architecture is needed.
